```
Build an interactive Merge Sort visualiser as a single-page static web app.

Layout and controls:
- A header titled "Merge Sort Visualiser" with a one-line explanation of how merge sort works.
- A control panel with: an "Array size" slider (5 to 50, default 16, id="size-slider"), a "Speed" slider (1 = slow to 10 = fast, default 5, id="speed-slider"), and buttons "New Array" (id="new-array-btn"), "Start" (id="start-btn"), "Pause"/"Resume" (id="pause-btn"), "Step" (id="step-btn", advances exactly one comparison or write while paused) and "Reset" (id="reset-btn").
- A text input (id="custom-input") with an "Apply" button (id="apply-btn") so I can type my own comma-separated numbers (e.g. "5, 3, 8, 1"). Show a clear inline error (id="input-error") for invalid input such as letters, empty values or more than 50 numbers.

Visualisation:
- Draw the array as vertical bars (container id="bars", each bar has data-testid="bar" and a data-value attribute holding its number) with heights proportional to their values and the value shown under each bar when there are 20 bars or fewer.
- Colour coding with a legend: default bars, the sub-array currently being merged (highlighted background range), the two elements being compared, an element being written into place, and fully sorted bars in green when finished.
- Show the current recursion depth and the left/mid/right indices of the active merge.
- A live stats panel: comparisons (id="comparisons-count"), array writes (id="writes-count"), and a status line (id="status") showing "Ready", "Sorting…", "Paused" or "Sorted!".
- A short log panel (id="step-log") listing the latest steps in plain English, e.g. "Comparing 7 and 3 → placing 3 at index 0", newest on top, limited to the last 15 entries.

Behaviour:
- Pre-compute the full list of merge sort steps first (compare / write / merge-range events), then animate through them, so Pause, Resume and Step work exactly and the final result is always correct.
- While sorting, disable New Array, Apply and the size slider; Reset stops the animation and restores the original unsorted array.
- Changing speed takes effect immediately during the animation.
- When finished, all bars turn green, the status reads "Sorted!" and the bars' data-value attributes are in ascending order.
- Keyboard shortcuts: Space toggles Start/Pause, the Right arrow key performs Step, R resets.

Design: a clean, modern, dark theme, responsive down to 360px wide (bars shrink and value labels hide on small screens), accessible labels on all controls and visible focus states. No external libraries are needed.

Tests to include (make them deterministic; use page.clock for animation timing and the custom input for known data):
1. Applying "5, 3, 8, 1" shows 4 bars with data-values 5, 3, 8, 1 in that order.
2. After applying "5, 3, 8, 1" and starting, fast-forwarding the clock makes the status "Sorted!" and the bars read 1, 3, 5, 8.
3. Step mode: after applying a custom array, pressing Step once increments the comparisons count to 1 and the status shows "Paused".
4. Invalid input "4, x, 2" shows the input error and does not change the bars.
5. Reset after sorting restores the original order.
6. The page loads without console errors.
```

Built a complete Merge Sort Visualiser as a single-page static web app. The app includes a header with explanation, control panel with sliders and buttons, custom array input with validation, animated bar visualisation with colour-coded legend, live stats panel, step log, and full keyboard support. The merge sort algorithm is pre-computed into discrete steps (compare, write, merge-range) for precise pause/resume/step control. Includes comprehensive Playwright tests covering custom input, sorting animation, step mode, invalid input handling, reset behaviour, and console error checking.
